title: How to Build a Talent Pipeline with an ATS (September 2026)
summary: Find out how to use an ATS to build a startup talent pipeline with smart tagging and fractional recruiting support. October 2026 guide.
body_markdown:
Building a[talent pipeline with an ATS](https://www.dover.com/) can change how quickly you fill roles. Most early-stage teams treat hiring as a reactive process, starting every search cold once a role opens. An ATS lets you build a reservoir of pre-vetted candidates you can tap immediately. This guide covers what to look for in a pipeline-ready ATS, how to set one up, and when fractional recruiting support makes sense.


**TLDR:**


-


An ATS helps startups store pre-vetted candidates you can resurface when roles open up.


-


Tagging candidates by role, skill, and stage lets you search existing contacts before sourcing.


-


Warm pipeline candidates can often shorten time-to-fill by skipping initial sourcing.


-


Fractional recruiters make sense when you’re juggling 3+ roles or stuck on senior searches.


-


Some recruiting tools combine fractional recruiting with ATS integration to build pipelines without full-time overhead.


## Why Startups Use an ATS to Build a Talent Pipeline


Startups move fast, so without a structured way to manage candidates, promising conversations get lost and roles stay open too long.


[An ATS](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-an-applicant-tracking-system) gives recruiting teams one place to track candidates across every hiring stage. Beyond daily hiring, it also builds a talent pipeline: pre-vetted candidates you can tap the moment a role opens.


### Why Pipeline Building Looks Different at Startups


-


Startups hire in bursts, so warm candidates in your ATS let you move fast once headcount opens.


-


The same recruiters or founders often juggle multiple roles, so organized candidate records carry real weight.


-


Smaller referral networks mean structured outreach tracked inside an ATS can expand your reach.


## What to Look for in an ATS Before You Build a Talent Pipeline


Not every ATS is built with pipeline-building in mind. Some track active applicants only, leaving you without the infrastructure to nurture candidates over time. Before committing to a tool, a pipeline-ready ATS should let you tag and segment candidates by role type, seniority, or stage so you can resurface the right people later.


It should also support automated outreach sequences, since manually following up with dozens of passive candidates isn’t sustainable at startup scale, and it should integrate with LinkedIn, job boards, and referral tools so candidate data flows in without manual entry.


### Questions to Ask Before You Commit


-


Does[the ATS](https://www.dover.com/blog/best-ats-systems) support custom stages beyond just “applied” and “rejected”?


-


Can you send templated follow-ups directly from the tool?


-


How easy is it to search your historical candidate database?


## How to Build a Talent Pipeline Using Your ATS


Building a talent pipeline with an ATS takes a deliberate system for categorizing, nurturing, and re-engaging candidates over time. Here is how to make that work as a startup.


### Set Up a Tagging and Segmentation System


Before sourcing anyone, build a tagging structure inside your ATS. Group candidates by role type, seniority, skill set, and pipeline stage. Consistent tagging means you can[search your existing candidate database](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-use-ats-hire-first-10-employees-startup) and surface people who already know your company.


### Automate Touchpoints Without Losing the Personal Feel


Most ATS tools let you schedule follow-up emails at set intervals. Use this to stay in touch with strong candidates who were not the right fit at the time. A short, personalized note every few months keeps your startup top of mind.


### Track Source Quality From the Start


Log where every candidate comes from and how far they progress. Over time,[core recruiting metrics](https://www.dover.com/blog/recruiting-metrics-for-startups) like source of hire show which channels produce the strongest pipeline, so you can put your budget where it performs.


## How Building a Talent Pipeline Fits Into Your Full Hiring Pipeline


A talent pipeline feeds into your broader hiring funnel, but the two serve different purposes. Your hiring pipeline covers active candidates moving through job requisitions right now. Your talent pipeline is the reservoir of warm, pre-vetted contacts you draw from when a role opens.


An ATS bridges both. It stores passive candidates alongside active applicants, giving recruiters a single place to revisit past finalists, silver medalists, and referrals who weren’t the right fit at the time but could be right six months later. Every role you fill from that existing pool cuts sourcing time considerably. According to[SHRM’s 2026 Recruiting Benchmarking data](https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/research/recruiting-benchmarking) , the median time-to-fill for nonexecutive positions is 39 calendar days.


## How AI Is Changing ATS Pipeline Building in 2026


Ashby’s 2026 State of Startup Hiring report found that about 60% of startup customers use AI functionality in Ashby, though most use only one or two features regularly. AI adoption is growing alongside hiring pressure: according to[GoodTime’s 2026 Hiring Insights](https://goodtime.io/blog/talent-operations/hiring-statistics/) , 60% of companies reported longer hiring timelines in 2025. For pipeline building, AI-generated personalization inside an ATS can help small teams send relevant follow-ups to passive candidates, where a generic check-in often gets ignored.[LinkedIn’s Future of Recruiting 2025 report](https://www.linkedin.com/business/talent/blog/talent-acquisition/future-of-recruiting-2025) found that TA professionals using generative AI reported a 20% reduction in overall workload. Bullhorn’s 2026 GRID Industry Trends Report found that 78% of staffing firms growing revenue by more than 25% have AI tools embedded directly in their ATS, compared to 51% of firms whose revenue declined by more than 10%. For startups without dedicated recruiting headcount, that gap favors an ATS with AI built in from the start.


## What Fall 2026 Hiring Trends Mean for Your Talent Pipeline


AI is making applications easier to produce and harder to tell apart. A recent[World Economic Forum roundup](https://www.weforum.org/stories/jobs-and-the-future-of-work/ai-hiring-recommendations-trends-jobs-skills-august-2026) describes an application arms race, with candidates using AI to tailor every submission while recruiters sort through near-identical résumés. It also notes that referrals may carry more weight as a result, since a personal recommendation offers a signal that an AI-written application cannot.


That trend raises the value of a warm, previously vetted pipeline. Tagging each candidate by how they were sourced, such as referral, past finalist, or outbound, lets you search that history first when a role opens. Polished applications are easier to fake too, so record in your ATS what a recruiter or hiring manager has actually confirmed in conversation, so the next search starts from verified signal instead of a résumé alone.


## When to Bring in a Fractional Recruiter to Support Building a Talent Pipeline


Think of the ATS as the foundation and[a fractional recruiter](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-a-fractional-recruiter-guide) as the capacity layer you add once sourcing bandwidth or role complexity outgrows what the tool alone can cover. An ATS handles organization, stage tracking, and nurturing well, but it can’t go find people, run judgment-based screens, or build a search for a function your team has never hired for. Those gaps are what a fractional recruiter fills.


[Fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-costs) plug in on top of your existing ATS to own sourcing outreach, configure pipeline stages, and run initial screens. Common triggers: roles open more than six weeks, thin inbound volume, or a new function the team hasn’t hired for. Once the search wraps, they hand off a warm pipeline, and the ATS keeps the full history for next time.


### Signs You’re Ready for Fractional Recruiting Support


-


You’re hiring for three or more roles at once and unreviewed applicants are piling up in your ATS.


-


Your pipeline has stalled on a senior or technical role, and generic sourcing isn’t producing qualified candidates.


-


You have an ATS set up but no one owns the process enough to move candidates quickly.


## The Cost of Getting Talent Pipeline Building Wrong as a Startup


Hiring mistakes hit startups harder than mature companies.[Research on bad-hire costs](https://www.socialtalent.com/blog/hiring/cost-of-a-bad-hire) suggests a bad hire can cost up to 30% of that employee’s first-year salary in direct expenses, before counting lost productivity and team morale.


Without a structured talent pipeline,[startups often default to reactive hiring](https://www.dover.com/blog/cost-of-hiring-agency-vs-in-house-vs-embedded-recruiting) , opening roles only once the need turns urgent.


The downstream effects compound quickly:


-


Roles stay open longer, pressuring existing team members and slowing execution.


-


Hiring managers re-screen pools instead of moving strong candidates forward.


-


Competitive candidates accept other offers while logistics are still being worked out.


An ATS gives startups the infrastructure to track candidates over time, so the groundwork is already done when a role opens.

DIY with ATS Only Very early stage teams with 1-2 roles per year and strong networks ATS subscription only, with some free tiers and paid plans that vary by features and user count Requires founder or hiring manager to own all sourcing, screening, and nurturing activities manually

## FAQs


### Do I need a recruiter if I’m already using an ATS?


An ATS alone is often enough if you have one or two open roles and a healthy inbound flow, since it organizes candidates, tracks stages, and keeps follow-up from slipping. The calculus changes once hiring grows to three or more roles at once, inbound slows, or you’re filling a senior search. At that point, a fractional recruiter layers on top of the ATS to own sourcing and screening.


### Can I build a talent pipeline without a full-time recruiter?


Yes. An ATS gives you the infrastructure to tag, segment, and nurture candidates over time, so you can maintain a warm pipeline without dedicated recruiting headcount. Most startups supplement their ATS with fractional recruiting support during hiring bursts, then scale back when needs change.


### How do I know if my ATS can actually support pipeline building?


Look for three things: custom tagging and segmentation beyond basic “applied” or “rejected” stages, automated follow-up sequences you can trigger from the tool itself, and searchable historical candidate databases. If your ATS only tracks active applicants through a single hiring process, it won’t give you what you need to nurture candidates over time.


### What should a company with under 50 employees look for in an ATS?


Teams under 50 employees often do well with an ATS that offers free or low-cost entry pricing, fast setup, and built-in tagging, search, and job multiposting. Tools built for large recruiting teams can feel heavy when no one owns recruiting full time. Check how pricing scales with headcount, since some tools price by company size or by seat.


## Final Thoughts on Building a Talent Pipeline as a Startup


Building a[talent pipeline with an ATS](https://www.dover.com/) gives a startup organization and memory, and a fractional recruiter adds sourcing capacity when volume or role complexity outgrows what software can cover alone. Where that balance lands depends on how many roles you are hiring for and how specialized they are. Dover’s model, for instance, pairs a free ATS with on-demand fractional recruiters in one shared system, so startups can build a warm, organized candidate pipeline without the overhead of a full-time recruiting function.
